title: Kenyan Sorghum Porridge
community: Popular in Western Kenya, Eastern Kenya, and pastoral communities
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Sorghum Porridge — uji wa mtama. Ground sorghum cooked into a warm, slightly reddish-brown porridge with a distinctive earthy, mildly smoky flavour. A deeply traditional Kenyan breakfast from communities where sorghum has been grown for thousands of years.
longDesc: Sorghum porridge has a distinctive character all its own — the slightly reddish-brown colour from the sorghum tannins, a subtle earthiness, and a mild smokiness that sets it apart from millet or maize porridge. In communities that have grown sorghum for generations, this porridge is associated with strength, resilience, and deep agricultural heritage.
steps: Mix sorghum flour with 1 cup cold water to a smooth slurry.
Bring remaining 3 cups water to a boil.
Pour slurry into boiling water while stirring constantly.
Stir over medium heat for 6—8 minutes until smooth and thickened.
Add sugar and milk if using. Simmer 2 more minutes.
chefTips: Sorghum porridge is thinner than millet porridge at the same ratio — it has a slightly more liquid consistency that many prefer.
Brown sugar or jaggery pairs particularly well with sorghum's earthy notes.
A combination of sorghum and millet flours creates a more complex flavour.
commonMistakes: Not making a slurry first — lumps.
Overcooking — becomes too thick and gluey.

faqs.q: How is sorghum porridge different from millet porridge?
faqs.a: Sorghum porridge has a slightly more earthy, mildly smoky character and a reddish-brown colour, while millet porridge is darker grey with a nuttier flavour. Both are nutritious and naturally gluten-free.

cookingScience: Sorghum flour has slightly coarser granules than finger millet, producing a slightly less smooth porridge at the same cooking time. The reddish colour comes from condensed tannins (proanthocyanidins) in the sorghum grain.
sustainabilityTips: Sorghum thrives in drought conditions — an excellent climate-resilient crop.
reheating: Add water and reheat gently, stirring.
healthBenefits: Rich in antioxidants from sorghum tannins.
Good source of iron and B vitamins.
culturalNote: Sorghum porridge is a breakfast that carries the memory of thousands of years of East African agriculture. In communities that have grown mtama for generations, a bowl of sorghum porridge in the morning is both nourishment and identity.
